newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO panel finds EU banana regime breaks rules.
newsitem.headline: WTO panel finds EU banana regime breaks rules.

text.p: A World Trade Organisation (WTO) dispute panel has ruled that the European Union's banana regime favouring imports from mainly Caribbean countries violate open trading rules, diplomats said on Tuesday.
The ruling essentially confirmed the findings of a preliminary report by the same three-man panel issued in March, according to the diplomats who had seen the report.
The panel said Brussels should bring its import regulations for bananas into line with the EU's obligations under global trade accords and WTO rules, the diplomats added.

The case against the regime had been brought to the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body by the United States, whose major banana-marketing companies say they have suffered discrimination costing them billions of dollars in lost trade.
But the U.S. also had the support of Mexico, Ecuador, Guatemala and Honduras.
The ruling, which the EU is expected to appeal, will come as a bitter blow to Caribbean banana producers like Jamaica, Belize, Surinam and the Windward Islands.
They say their economies could be devastated if the preferences they enjoy under the EU regime are withdrawn and cheaper Latin American bananas flood the European market.
